concepts.title: Integration of Princely States
concepts.definition: At independence in 1947, India had over 500 princely states. Integration was the process by which these states acceded to the Indian Union, forming a unified nation.
concepts.key_idea: Most princely states joined India through persuasion and agreements; a few required special measures.
question_patterns: explain the process of integration of princely states
list the challenges in integrating princely states
describe how Hyderabad joined the Indian Union
compare accession of Junagadh and Hyderabad
justify the need for integration of princely states

solution_steps.explain: At independence, British India was partitioned and princely states had to choose to join India or Pakistan.
Most states acceded through persuasion and instruments of accession; some like Hyderabad, Junagadh, and Kashmir required special action.
By 1949-50, almost all princely states had merged into the Indian Union, creating a unified India.

worked_examples.question: How did the princely state of Hyderabad join the Indian Union?
worked_examples.solution: The Nizam of Hyderabad refused to join India. In September 1948, the Indian government launched a police action called Operation Polo, and Hyderabad acceded to India.
worked_examples.answer: Hyderabad joined through Operation Polo in 1948.

concepts.title: States Reorganisation Act 1956
concepts.definition: The States Reorganisation Act 1956 was a law that reorganised the boundaries of Indian states on the basis of language, reducing the number of states and creating a more rational administrative structure.
concepts.key_idea: The Act redrew state boundaries primarily along linguistic lines, replacing the earlier arrangement inherited from British rule.
question_patterns: explain the purpose of the States Reorganisation Act 1956
describe the basis on which states were reorganised in 1956
list states created by the 1956 Act
compare state boundaries before and after 1956
justify the need for reorganisation of states

solution_steps.explain: Note that the Act used language as the primary basis.
List the states formed or merged by the Act.
State how the Act changed the political map.

worked_examples.question: On what basis were states reorganised by the States Reorganisation Act 1956?
worked_examples.solution: The Act reorganised states primarily on the basis of language, so that people speaking the same language were grouped in one state.

worked_examples.question: Name two states created by the 1956 reorganisation.
worked_examples.solution: Andhra Pradesh (for Telugu speakers) and Bombay State (later split) were among the states affected by the 1956 Act.

concepts.title: Formation of Linguistic States
concepts.definition: Linguistic states are states organised so that people speaking a common language form a single administrative unit. Andhra Pradesh was the first linguistic state, formed in 1953 after the fasting death of Potti Sriramulu.
concepts.key_idea: Creating linguistic states made administration easier and strengthened democratic participation by respecting language identity.
question_patterns: explain how Andhra Pradesh became the first linguistic state
describe the role of Potti Sriramulu
list advantages of linguistic states
compare linguistic and non-linguistic state organisation
justify the demand for linguistic states

solution_steps.action: State the demand for linguistic states
solution_steps.explain: People wanted states organised by language so that administration and education could use their mother tongue.
Potti Sriramulu fasted for a separate Andhra state; his death in 1953 led to the creation of Andhra Pradesh, the first linguistic state.
The success of Andhra Pradesh led to the States Reorganisation Act 1956, creating more linguistic states.

worked_examples.question: How was Andhra Pradesh formed as the first linguistic state?
worked_examples.solution: Potti Sriramulu went on a fast demanding a separate state for Telugu speakers. After his death in 1953, Andhra Pradesh was created, becoming the first linguistic state.
worked_examples.answer: Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's fast.

concepts.title: Boundary Changes and Their Reasons
concepts.definition: Boundary changes are alterations to the borders of states or creation of new states to improve administration, address linguistic or cultural identity, or meet regional demands.
concepts.key_idea: Boundaries change over time due to linguistic demands, administrative convenience, and regional movements.
question_patterns: explain reasons for boundary changes in India
describe how a new state is created
list states created after 2000
compare boundary changes in 1956 and 2000
justify the creation of a new state from a larger one

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the change was due to language, administration, or regional demand.
List the states created or merged.

worked_examples.question: Name three states created in the year 2000 and state the reason for each.
worked_examples.solution: Chhattisgarh (from Madhya Pradesh), Uttaranchal (now Uttarakhand, from Uttar Pradesh), and Jharkhand (from Bihar) were created in 2000 to improve administration and address regional demands.
worked_examples.answer: Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand -- created for administrative and regional reasons

worked_examples.answer: On linguistic grounds -- Gujarati speakers wanted a separate state

concepts.title: Union Territories
concepts.definition: Union Territories are regions administered directly by the Central Government of India. They do not have the full powers of a state and are governed by an administrator or Lieutenant Governor.
concepts.key_idea: Union Territories are created for strategic, cultural, or administrative reasons where direct central control is preferred.

worked_examples.question: Why is Chandigarh a Union Territory?

worked_examples.answer: Because it is the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana

concepts.title: Administrative Divisions of India
concepts.definition: India is administratively divided into states and Union Territories. States are further divided into districts, and districts into tehsils or blocks for governance.
concepts.key_idea: The administrative hierarchy flows from the Centre to states to districts to local bodies, enabling governance at each level.

concepts.title: Current Political Map of India
concepts.definition: The current political map of India shows 28 states and 8 Union Territories, reflecting the latest boundary changes including the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.
concepts.key_idea: The political map changes with the creation of new states and Union Territories; the latest major change was in 2019 with Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
question_patterns: identify states on the political map of India

describe the 2019 reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir

solution_steps.explain: India currently has 28 states and 8 Union Territories.
In 2019, Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised into two Union Territories: Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
The political map continues to evolve with administrative and regional demands.
